name: Curcumin
text:
Curcumin is the yellow-orange pigment of turmeric, extracted from the root of the plant Curcuma longa. It is used to colour mustard, curry powders, dairy products, baked goods, confectionery and drinks.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Riboflavin
text:
Riboflavin is vitamin B2, formerly called lactoflavin. It occurs naturally in milk, eggs and liver, and the additive is usually produced by fermentation or synthesis. It gives a yellow-orange colour and is also used to fortify foods, for example in cereals, dairy products, sauces and drinks. The E101(i) form is riboflavin itself and the (ii) form is riboflavin-5'-phosphate.

Regulatory status: approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Tartrazine
text:
Tartrazine is a synthetic lemon-yellow azo dye, also known in the US as FD&C Yellow 5. It is used in soft drinks, sweets, desserts, sauces, snacks and coated products.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US. Products in the EU and UK require a warning label, and its use is described as being phased out there. The label warns that the colour may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children. Some sensitive people may also react to it with skin or respiratory symptoms.

name: Alkannin
text:
Alkannin is a red-brown natural pigment obtained from the roots of alkanet (Alkanna tinctoria). It has been used mainly as a dye for cosmetics, textiles and some foods, but it is rarely encountered in food today.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US, so it should not be present in foods sold in those markets.

name: Quinoline Yellow
text:
Quinoline Yellow WS is a synthetic dye that gives a dull or greenish yellow colour. It is used in sweets, desserts, soft drinks, smoked fish coatings and similar products where permitted.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. Products in the EU and UK require a warning label saying the colour may affect activity and attention in children, and its use is described as being phased out. It is not approved in the US.

name: Fast Yellow AB
text:
Fast Yellow AB is a synthetic yellow azo dye that was once used as a food colour. It is no longer in use as a food additive, and little current information about it is available.

It is forbidden in the EU, the UK and the US, so it does not appear in foods sold in these markets.

name: Riboflavin-5'-sodium phosphate
text:
Riboflavin-5'-sodium phosphate is the sodium salt of the phosphate ester of riboflavin (vitamin B2). It is a yellow, water-soluble form of the vitamin that can be used as a food colour and as a source of vitamin B2.

It is closely related to E101a and has no individual record of its own. No separate EU, UK or US approval status is recorded for it.

name: Yellow 2G
text:
Yellow 2G is a synthetic yellow azo dye. It was used in the past to colour foods, but it is now obsolete as a food additive.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US, so it should not be found in foods in those markets.

name: Sunset Yellow FCF
text:
Sunset Yellow FCF, also called Orange Yellow S or FD&C Yellow 6, is a synthetic yellow-orange azo dye. It is used in soft drinks, sweets, desserts, snacks, sauces and baked goods.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US. Products in the EU and UK require a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children, and its use is being phased out there. It is also banned in Norway.

name: Orange GGN
text:
Orange GGN is a synthetic orange azo dye that was once used to colour foods. It is no longer used as a food additive and there is little current information about it.

It is forbidden in the EU, the UK and the US.

name: Carmine (cochineal)
text:
Cochineal, carminic acid and carmine (Natural Red 4) are crimson pigments obtained from the dried bodies of the cochineal insect, which lives on cacti. This is an animal-derived colour, so it is not suitable for vegetarians and vegans.

It is used in drinks, yoghurts, sweets, meat products and sauces. It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US. Carmine can rarely cause allergic reactions in sensitive people.

name: Citrus Red 2
text:
Citrus Red 2 is a synthetic orange to pink dye. Its use is very narrow: it colours the skin of some oranges and is not applied to the edible part.

It is approved in the US only for colouring the skin of oranges. It is not approved in the EU and the UK.

name: Carmoisine
text:
Carmoisine, also called azorubine, is a synthetic azo dye that gives a red to maroon colour. It is used in sweets, jellies, desserts, drinks and baked goods.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. Products in the EU and UK require a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children, and its use is being phased out. It is also banned in Canada, Japan, Norway and the USA.

name: Amaranth
text:
Amaranth, also known as FD&C Red 2, is a synthetic red azo dye. It is not related to the amaranth plant. It has been used in drinks, sweets, desserts and some alcoholic products.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK, but banned in the United States.

name: Ponceau 4R
text:
Ponceau 4R, also called Cochineal Red A or Brilliant Scarlet 4R, is a synthetic pink-red azo dye. Despite the name, it is not made from cochineal. It is used in sweets, desserts, soft drinks and processed meat or fish products.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. Products in the EU and UK require a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children, and its use is being phased out. It is not approved in the US.

name: Ponceau SX
text:
Ponceau SX, also called Scarlet GN, is a synthetic red azo dye. It is not a common food colour today, and little current information about its food use is available.

In the US it is permitted only for externally applied drugs and cosmetics. It is not approved in the EU and the UK, so it should not be present in foods there.

name: Ponceau 6R
text:
Ponceau 6R is a synthetic red azo dye. It is an obsolete food colour about which little current information is available.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK. No US approval status is recorded for it.

name: Erythrosine
text:
Erythrosine, also known as FD&C Red 3, is a synthetic pink-red dye based on iodine. It is best known for colouring cocktail and glace cherries, and it has also been used in sweets and baked goods.

It is approved in the UK and approved in the EU for cocktail, candied and bigareaux cherries only. It is banned in the US.

name: Red 2G
text:
Red 2G is a synthetic red or pink azo dye that was once used to colour foods such as sausages and preserves. It is now obsolete as a food additive.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Allura Red AC
text:
Allura Red AC, also known as FD&C Red 40, is a synthetic red azo dye. It is one of the most widely used red colours, found in soft drinks, sweets, desserts, sauces, snacks and cereals.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US. Products in the EU and UK require a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children, and its use is being phased out. It is also banned in several individual countries.

name: Indanthrene blue RS
text:
Indanthrene blue RS is a synthetic blue vat dye, an anthraquinone-type pigment better known as a textile dye than as a food colour. Little is documented about its use in food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US, so it should not be present in foods in those markets.

name: Patent Blue V
text:
Patent Blue V is a synthetic sky-blue dye of the triarylmethane group. In food it has been used in a few products, such as some preserves and confectionery.

It is approved in the EU for preserves of red fruit only and approved in the UK. It is banned in the US and Australia.

name: Indigo carmine
text:
Indigo carmine, also called indigotine or FD&C Blue 2, is a synthetic dye related to the natural indigo, giving a deep blue colour. It is used in sweets, ice cream, drinks, baked goods and pet food.

It is approved in the EU and the UK and approved in the US.

name: Brilliant Blue FCF
text:
Brilliant Blue FCF, also known as FD&C Blue 1, is a synthetic blue dye of the triarylmethane group. It is used alone or mixed with yellow dyes to make green, in drinks, sweets, ice cream, dairy desserts and canned peas.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Chlorophylls
text:
Chlorophylls and chlorophyllins are the green pigments of plants, commonly extracted from grass, alfalfa or nettle. Chlorophyllins are the water-soluble derivatives made from the natural pigment.

They give a green colour to sweets, ice cream, drinks, sauces and other foods. They are approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Copper complexes of chlorophylls
text:
Copper complexes of chlorophylls and chlorophyllins are made from natural chlorophyll by replacing the central magnesium with copper. This gives a more stable, brighter green colour than the natural pigment. They are used in sweets, ice cream, soups and drinks.

They are approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. In the US they are approved for citrus-based dry beverage mixes.

name: Green S
text:
Green S is a synthetic green dye of the triarylmethane group, also known as Acid Brilliant Green BS. It has been used in sweets, desserts, mint sauce and some drinks.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. It is not approved in the US.

name: Fast Green FCF
text:
Fast Green FCF, also known as FD&C Green 3, is a synthetic turquoise-green dye of the triarylmethane group. It has been used in food and drinks, and also in cosmetics and as a biological stain.

It is approved in the US and not approved in the EU and the UK.

name: Plain caramel
text:
Plain caramel (caramel I) is a brown colour made by heating sugars, without ammonia or sulfite compounds. It is the simplest of the four caramel colour classes and is used in spirits, sauces, baked goods and confectionery.

It is approved in the EU only in seaweed-based fish roe analogues, and only E150a made from honey for a specific type of mead. It is approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Caustic sulfite caramel
text:
Caustic sulfite caramel (caramel II) is a brown colour made by heating sugars with sulfite compounds in the presence of an alkali, but without ammonia. It is used in drinks such as fortified wines and spirits, and in some other foods.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Ammonia caramel
text:
Ammonia caramel (caramel III) is a brown colour made by heating sugars with ammonia compounds. It is used in products such as beer, malt beverages, breakfast cereals, sauces and baked goods.

It is approved in the EU only for breakfast cereals and for beer and malt beverages, with conditions. It is approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Sulfite ammonia caramel
text:
Sulfite ammonia caramel (caramel IV) is a brown colour made by heating sugars with both sulfite and ammonia compounds. It is the caramel colour most often used in soft drinks, particularly colas, and also in sauces, vinegars and spirits.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Brilliant Black BN
text:
Brilliant Black BN, also called Black PN, is a synthetic black azo dye. It has been used in sauces, desserts, fish roe substitutes, confectionery and drinks where permitted.

It is approved in the EU only in processed seafood, with conditions. It is approved in the UK, and banned in the US.

name: Carbon black
text:
Carbon black (hydrocarbon black) is a black pigment made by the incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons. It was once used as a food colour but is now rarely encountered, and it is known mainly as an industrial pigment.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Vegetable carbon
text:
Vegetable carbon is a black pigment made by charring plant material such as wood or peat. It is used in confectionery, liquorice-type sweets, cheese rind and some decorative products.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. It is banned in the US.

name: Brown FK
text:
Brown FK, called kipper brown, is a synthetic mixture of azo dyes that gives a brown colour. It was used only for dyeing smoked fish, known as kippers.

The EU approval was withdrawn in November 2011. It is not approved in the UK or the US.

name: Brown HT
text:
Brown HT, also called chocolate brown HT, is a synthetic brown azo dye. It has been used in chocolate-flavoured cakes, confectionery, sauces and some other foods.

It is approved in the EU in precooked crustaceans and in fresh meat only for the purpose of health marking. It is approved in the UK and not approved in the US.

name: Carotenes
text:
Carotenes (alpha-, beta- and gamma-carotene) are yellow-orange pigments found in carrots, palm oil and many other plants. The additive can be extracted from plants or algae, or produced synthetically. Beta-carotene is also a precursor of vitamin A.

It colours margarine, cheese, drinks, baked goods and confectionery. It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. In the US only beta-carotene is approved.

name: Annatto
text:
Annatto is an orange natural colour extracted from the seeds of the achiote tree (Bixa orellana). Its main pigments are bixin, which is fat-soluble, and norbixin, which is water-soluble.

It is widely used to colour cheese, butter, margarine, snacks, smoked fish and cereals. It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US. Rare allergic reactions to annatto have been reported.

name: Paprika extract
text:
Paprika extract is a red natural colour obtained from the ripe fruits of the red pepper Capsicum annuum. Its main pigments are capsanthin and capsorubin. It is used in sausages, sauces, snacks, cheese, soups and seasoning blends.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Lycopene
text:
Lycopene is the red carotenoid pigment of tomatoes, watermelon and pink grapefruit. The additive is extracted from tomatoes or produced by fermentation or chemical synthesis.

It gives colour to drinks, sauces, soups, desserts and meat products. It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Beta-apo-8'-carotenal
text:
Beta-apo-8'-carotenal is an orange-red to yellow carotenoid pigment. It occurs in small amounts in citrus fruit and spinach, but the additive is normally made synthetically. It is used in cheese, soups, sauces, drinks and baked goods.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Ethyl ester of beta-apo-8'-carotenic acid
text:
The ethyl ester of beta-apo-8'-carotenic acid is a synthetic carotenoid-type pigment giving an orange-red to yellow colour. It is closely related to E160e. It is little used today and little current information is available.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Flavoxanthin
text:
Flavoxanthin is a golden-yellow carotenoid pigment of the xanthophyll group, found in some flowers such as buttercups. It has hardly any practical use as a food colour.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Lutein
text:
Lutein is a yellow to orange-red carotenoid pigment found in marigold flowers, green leafy vegetables and egg yolk. The additive is usually extracted from marigold petals. It is used to colour dairy products, baked goods, drinks, and also animal feed.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. In the US it is approved for chicken feed only.

name: Cryptoxanthin
text:
Cryptoxanthin is an orange-red carotenoid pigment found in fruits such as papaya, oranges and red peppers. It is a precursor of vitamin A, but it is not used as a food colour in practice.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Rubixanthin
text:
Rubixanthin is an orange-red carotenoid pigment found in rose hips and some other plants. It is of mainly scientific interest and is not a practical food colour.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Violaxanthin
text:
Violaxanthin is an orange carotenoid pigment found in many green plants and in some flowers, such as pansies. It is not used as a practical food colour.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Rhodoxanthin
text:
Rhodoxanthin is a carotenoid pigment found in some conifers, yews and a few other plants, which gives a deep red to purple colour. It has no practical use as a food colour.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Canthaxanthin
text:
Canthaxanthin is a carotenoid pigment found in some mushrooms, crustaceans and fish. The additive is made synthetically. It has been used to colour animal feed, for example to deepen the colour of egg yolks and of farmed salmon flesh.

It is approved in the EU for medicinal products only, approved in the UK and approved in the US. High intakes have been associated with deposits in the retina.

name: Zeaxanthin
text:
Zeaxanthin is a yellow-orange carotenoid pigment found in maize, paprika, egg yolk and many leafy vegetables. It is present in the human retina together with lutein.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US as a food colour with this number.

name: Citranaxanthin
text:
Citranaxanthin is a synthetic carotenoid-type pigment that gives a deep yellow to orange colour. It is used mainly in poultry feed to colour egg yolks and skin, and little is documented about its use in human food.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.

name: Astaxanthin
text:
Astaxanthin is a red carotenoid pigment found in algae, shrimp, krill and salmon, to which it gives their pink-red colour. It is produced from algae or yeast, or synthetically.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK as a food additive. In the US it is approved for salmonid fish feed only.

name: Beetroot red
text:
Beetroot red, whose main pigment is betanin, is a red natural colour extracted from red beet (Beta vulgaris). It is sensitive to heat, light and oxygen, so it is used mainly in products that are not heated for long, such as ice cream, yoghurt, desserts, sweets and sauces.

It is approved in the EU with conditions, approved in the UK and approved in the US.

name: Anthocyanins
text:
Anthocyanins are water-soluble plant pigments responsible for the red, purple and blue colours of berries, grapes, red cabbage, purple carrots and many flowers. Their colour depends on acidity, giving red in acid conditions and bluish or green shades as the pH rises.

They are used in drinks, confectionery, jams and dairy products. They are approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. In the US, grape extract anthocyanin is approved for beverages only.

name: Saffron
text:
Saffron is a spice made from the dried stigmas of the crocus flower (Crocus sativus). Its pigment, crocin, gives dishes a yellow-orange colour, and it is also a flavouring. It is one of the most expensive spices in the world.

It is not approved in the EU and the UK as an additive with this number. In the US it is approved.

name: Calcium carbonate
text:
Calcium carbonate is a white mineral compound that occurs naturally as chalk, limestone and marble, and is also produced industrially. As a food additive it works as a white colour and as an anticaking agent, acidity regulator and calcium supplement. It is used in confectionery, bread flour, dairy alternatives and supplements.

It is approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. In the US it is approved for dietary supplements, candies and chewing gum only.

name: Titanium dioxide
text:
Titanium dioxide is a white mineral pigment, made from titanium ores. It was used to whiten and brighten confectionery, chewing gum, sauces, icing and coatings, and also in medicines and cosmetics.

It is no longer approved in the EU for food products as of June 2022, because of the identification of potential carcinogenic effects. It remains approved in the EU for medicinal products only. It is approved in the UK, except Northern Ireland, and approved in the US for specific foods.

name: Iron oxides and hydroxides
text:
Iron oxides and iron hydroxides are mineral pigments, produced synthetically, which give yellow, red, brown or black shades. They are used in confectionery, pet food, sausage casings, supplements and decorations.

They are approved in the EU with conditions and approved in the UK. In the US they are approved for sausage casings, dietary supplements, candies and chewing gum.

name: Aluminium
text:
Aluminium used as an additive is a fine silver-grey metallic powder. It is used to give a metallic finish to the surface of products such as sugar confectionery and cake decorations.

It is approved in the EU only for external coatings of sugar confectionery. It is approved in the UK and not approved in the US.

name: Silver
text:
Silver, used as a food additive, is the metal in a very thin leaf or powder. It is applied only as a decorative silver surface on products such as confectionery, chocolates and liqueurs, and it passes through the body without being used.

It is approved in the EU only for external coatings of confectionery and for decoration of chocolates and liqueurs. It is approved in the UK and not approved in the US.

name: Gold
text:
Gold, used as a food additive, is the metal in the form of very thin leaf or powder. It is used purely for decoration, for example on chocolates, confectionery, liqueurs and luxury desserts. Gold is chemically inert, so it is not digested.

It is approved in the EU only for external coatings of confectionery and for decoration of chocolates and liqueurs. It is approved in the UK and not approved in the US.

name: Lithol Rubine BK
text:
Lithol Rubine BK, also called Pigment Rubine, is a synthetic red azo pigment (a calcium salt). It is used in a very narrow way, for colouring the rind of some cheeses.

It is approved in the EU only in edible cheese rind, with conditions. It is approved in the UK and not approved in the US.

name: Tannin
text:
Tannins are natural plant substances found in oak bark, galls, tea, grapes and many other plants. They give a brown colour and astringency. They are also used as clarifying agents, for example in wine and beer production.

Tannin is not approved in the EU and the UK as an additive with this number. It is approved in the US.

name: Orcein
text:
Orcein, also called orchil, is a purple natural dye obtained from lichens by treating them with ammonia in the presence of air. It is better known as a textile dye and a biological stain than as a food colour.

It is not approved in the EU, the UK or the US.
